target: Headline break-even $0.5B (CFG-1 technology licensing at 20 bps)
finding: The lowest headline ($0.48-0.51B) is CFG-1, which is software licensing only: the sponsor does all administration. Charging 20 bps of AUA for software alone is unsupported. At a $250k balance, 20 bps is $500 per account per year, about 6x the incumbent scale price of $81 per account that the original model used for licensing (MD-6). The original also lists 'buyers pay < ~$60 per account' as a thesis-invalidating signal. A sponsor COO would benchmark against per-account licence prices, not against full-administration bps.
proposed_correction: Price CFG-1/CFG-2 at an evidenced licence price (per-account $60-150, or 3-6 bps equivalent) and keep 20 bps only for CFG-4/5 full administration. Report licensing break-even at 5 bps or $81/acct alongside the 20 bps figure.
change_or_reason: REV-A: licensing-per-account.csv; licensing reported at per-account prices; 20 bps licensing labelled unrealistic

target: sponsorsFor = assets/$500M (Outputs.fs line 21); break-even $0.5B and 'minimum viable sponsor $75-100M'
finding: Every break-even curve assumes an average sponsor of $500M, so $0.5B break-even means one $500M sponsor. The two headline claims contradict each other. If the book is built from $75-100M sponsors (the claimed minimum viable size), each one adds about $70-130k of per-sponsor cost: tenant, onboarding share, quarterly reports, training and QBRs. Contribution per $100M sponsor at 20 bps is only about $71k.
proposed_correction: Add sponsor-size as an explicit break-even dimension (e.g. $50M, $100M, $250M, $500M sponsors) and state break-even as a number of sponsors of a given size. Retire the single $0.5B headline, or qualify it as 'one $500M sponsor'.
change_or_reason: REV-A: break-even-by-sponsor-size.csv; headlines state sponsor size

target: sponsor-unit-economics.csv onboarding_hours (Outputs.fs lines 256-260)
finding: The onboarding hours per sponsor (791.66 h, $95k) are mislabelled. They are the annualised PerSponsorOnboarding load of the 'plus' scenario: 3 sponsors x new_sponsor_share 0.2 = 0.6 onboardings per year (Volume.fs line 72: PerSponsorOnboarding -> NewSponsors). They are not the effort for one sponsor. True per-sponsor onboarding is about 791.66/0.6 = 1,320 h. Pricing all hours at a flat $120/h also understates the controller, compliance and executive time involved ($190-250/h fractional).
proposed_correction: Compute onboarding for one sponsor (divide by NewSponsors, or evaluate with NewSponsors = 1), cost it at pool rates, and recompute payback and minimum viable sponsor size.
change_or_reason: REV-A: onboarding hours per sponsor computed per event (1,319 h)

target: Founder availability: founder_hours_per_year 400 (ZBP-016) and founderAllocation
finding: One person has about 1,800 h/yr across 30 initiatives, an average of about 60 h per initiative. The base of 400 h (22% of all founder time) has no owner allocation decision behind it (the ZBP-016 source says so). More founder work sits outside the 400 h cap: shared component maintenance FC-101 is 'founder-performed so non-cash' ($52.5k = about 260 h at $200/h); the shared assurance programme FC-105 adds $45k; development FC-301/302 is a founder-plus-agent build; and in any year a sponsor is won, about 1,300 h of sales and onboarding falls due. Realistic Unbound demand on the founder is about 900-1,500 h, 50-80% of all capacity, which is incompatible with 29 other initiatives.
proposed_correction: Obtain an owner allocation (calendar commitment) for Unbound. Add every founder-performed line (FC-101, FC-105, build, acquisition-year sales and onboarding) to one founder-hours budget, and convert any excess over the allocation to cash hires in View 1.
change_or_reason: Founder sensitivity 0-1,800 h output; base 400 h retained as ASSUMPTION; escalated as owner decision OD-ZB-01

target: Key-person risk: single human holds every role (product owner, 'board', pricing, engineering approver)
finding: There is one human identity across all repositories (5,609 commits). The owner acts 'as Unbound board', and no Unbound entity exists. CNV-PLT-010 needs an author plus two non-author approvers, and the model fills one of the three engineering named persons with the founder. If the founder is absent, change control, on-call cover, pricing authority and contract signature all stop. A procurement team would require: key-person and continuity plans, source-code escrow with verification, named successors, documented runbooks, and evidence of a second accountable executive. None is costed.
proposed_correction: Add cost lines for escrow (about $5-15k/yr including verification), key-person insurance (about $3-10k/yr), a contracted second executive or GM retainer (about $50-120k/yr), and BCP tabletop exercises. Add a scenario with founder hours = 0 in which the third engineer is hired.
change_or_reason: REV-B: FC-022 key-person continuity; named-person minimums

target: SOC 1 Type II activation (FC-005 vendor_controls only; CFG-1/CFG-2/CFG-6 exempt)
finding: SOC 1 is costed only when the vendor performs controls (CFG-3 to CFG-5). But in CFG-1/2 the hosted platform keeps the fund ledger, computes balances and creates ACH files (platform_creates_ach_files = 1, TPSP). That processing is relevant to the sponsor's ICFR, so the sponsor's auditor will ask for a SOC 1 Type II even for software-only licensing. A Type II report also needs a 6-12 month observation period before it can be issued, which delays the first contract. The model has no time dimension for this.
proposed_correction: Activate FC-005 for every hosted configuration that keeps the book of record or creates payment files. Add the observation period to time-to-first-revenue and to pre-revenue burn.
change_or_reason: REV-A: SOC 1 active whenever a sponsor relies on the platform (FC-005)

target: Pre-revenue burn and working capital: months_to_first_revenue, receivable_arrears_months, contract_term_years are dead parameters
finding: Three commercial parameters are defined in parameters.csv but referenced nowhere in model/src: ZBP-041 months_to_first_revenue (6/12/18), ZBP-040 receivable_arrears_months, and ZBP-039 contract_term_years. The 'with investment' break-even amortises only the one-time lines FC-301/303/304 (Outputs.fs amortisedInvestment). It omits the operating cost incurred before the first fee: 2 dedicated engineers from the first account, assurance, insurance and SOC observation. The original model recorded 9-24 month sales cycles.
proposed_correction: Model a launch phase: months to first revenue x View 1 run-rate, plus receivables, as capital to recover. Add it to the development investment and to the amortised break-even. Show a cash-trough figure.
change_or_reason: REV-A: capital-required.csv uses months_to_first_revenue and receivables

target: Development investment FC-301 $0.5M cash / FC-302 $1.5M economic
finding: Unbound has no product application code. It has 27k F# lines, mostly requirements and economics tooling, plus one incubating library; there is no CI and no hosting choice. A regulated multi-tenant ledger with payments, RLS isolation, SOC-grade change control and migration tooling is costed at $150k-1.2M cash on the assumption that the founder and agents build it largely for free. The Unbound repository's own build_capex assumption is $5M ($3-15M). The original baseline build range is $1.1-2.43M. The build also needs founder hours that the 400 h cap cannot hold.
proposed_correction: Use an independent bottom-up build estimate for release 1. Treat $0.5M as a floor, not a base. Show the economic case at $1.5-5M and test the investment-recovery break-even at the high end.
change_or_reason: Recorded in 16; FC-301/302 retained wide; CI/CD build noted as one-time

target: Revenue concentration at break-even (stress.csv only tests 4 sponsors at $1B)
finding: At the $0.5B headline the business has exactly one sponsor, so 100% of revenue sits with one contract. The concentration stress is run only at $1B with 4 sponsors; there, losing a 40%-of-assets sponsor already turns View 1 negative (-$38k). No churn, non-renewal or termination-for-convenience is modelled. contract_term_years is unused, and sponsor count is never reduced in the Monte Carlo.
proposed_correction: Report a largest-sponsor share at each break-even point. Add annual churn or non-renewal probability (e.g. 5-15%) and model the loss of the only sponsor (revenue to 0, cost to the fixed floor of about $0.9M). State a diversification threshold, e.g. no sponsor above 33%, for the investment case.
change_or_reason: Concentration in 18/19; stress and sponsor-size tables

target: CAC and sales effort: cac_cash_per_sponsor $20k plus OA-COM-001 200 h per won sponsor; new_sponsor_share 0.2
finding: Acquisition is costed at $20k cash plus 200 h of sales per won sponsor (OA-COM-001, 12,000 min, freq 1). Lost pursuits count only for RFP/DDQ responses. In annual opex these hours are multiplied by new_sponsor_share 0.2, so at 1 sponsor the model carries 0.2 of one sale per year: COMM is only 86 h. The original model used a CAC of $125k ($60-250k). It also found that only 1 of 26 national and faith sponsors left Ren's platform in 2023-26, with sales cycles of 9-24 months. A 20-30% win rate implies 3-5 full pursuits per win.
proposed_correction: Set CAC as fully loaded cost per win (pursuits per win x hours per pursuit + cash), with base near $100-150k. Model the years when sponsor count grows explicitly, not as a steady-state 20% share.
change_or_reason: REV-B: CAC cash raised to 10/30/80k for lost pursuits

target: Insurance limits FC-001/002/003 (cyber $15k, tech E&O $12k, crime $8k base)
finding: A sponsor administering $100M-1B of charitable assets and donor PII, with a vendor creating ACH files, will usually contract for cyber, tech E&O and crime/FTF limits in the $5-10M range, plus additional-insured status and a vendor-fraud endorsement. Combined base premiums of $35k for a pre-revenue single-founder vendor with no loss history or SOC report are optimistic. D&O is costed only in the standalone G&A view.
proposed_correction: Cost insurance to stated contractual limits (e.g. $5M cyber / $5M E&O / $2-5M crime). Use the high column as base until a broker indication exists, and add D&O to View 1 once outside directors or investors exist.
change_or_reason: REV-A: insurance ranges raised for $3-5M limits

target: Staffed support and SLA (CFG-1 support share 0.1; no SLA credits; on-call staffed by 2 engineers + founder)
finding: Under CFG-1 the vendor answers only tier-2 platform tickets (support 0.1). Institutional buyers normally require staffed business-hours support, a named customer success manager, 24x7 Sev-1 response, published uptime SLAs with service credits, and December peak cover. The model has no service-credit liability. A 1-in-3 on-call rotation in which one person is the founder serving 30 initiatives cannot be sustained, and auditors will see it as such.
proposed_correction: Add a minimum support floor for every configuration (e.g. 0.5 FTE support/CSM), an on-call stipend or a fourth rotation member, and a revenue haircut for expected SLA credits (e.g. 2-5% of fees at risk).
change_or_reason: CFG-2 is the realistic licensing offer; CFG-1 kept as boundary case

target: Exit, portability and vendor-failure protections
finding: OA-COM-015 covers orderly sponsor exits (0.05 per sponsor per year). The model does not cost what a buyer will require against vendor failure: source and data escrow with release triggers, contractual transition assistance (typically 6-12 months of run-off service at the incumbent's price), audited vendor financial statements, and evidence of runway (often 18-24 months of cash). For a founder-only vendor with no Unbound entity, buyers will discount this risk heavily.
proposed_correction: Add escrow, an annual financial-statement audit (about $20-40k), a transition-assistance reserve, and a minimum runway capital requirement to the investor case.
change_or_reason: REV-B: FC-021 escrow and continuity

target: References and first-customer terms (OD-M-14: no design partner)
finding: The owner has decided there will be no design-partner sponsor and that handling times will come from an internal synthetic time study, which has not run. A COO will want referenceable production clients, a passed security review and SOC history. Without references, the first sponsor normally needs pilot pricing, fee holidays, performance guarantees or termination rights, and some buyers will not engage at all. The model charges full 20 bps from the first day of the first sponsor.
proposed_correction: Model first-sponsor concessions (e.g. 25-50% fee discount for 12-24 months, or a capped fee) and a probability of no first sale within the horizon, as part of launch economics.
change_or_reason: Evidence gap; validation plan (25) puts time study and design partner first

target: Like-for-like: buyer total cost of ownership vs 20 bps fee
finding: Even under full administration (CFG-5), about 2,631 sponsor hours per year ($184k at $70/h) stay with the sponsor at $500M: reserved decisions, activation gates, auditor planned approach. In CFG-1 the sponsor carries about 3,700 h. A buyer compares fee plus retained labour plus migration and activation burden against the incumbent all-in price. The vendor's revenue headroom at 20 bps is therefore smaller than the model implies.
proposed_correction: Present buyer TCO (fee + sponsor labour + migration) as bps, and test the fee the buyer can bear net of retained labour.
change_or_reason: REV-A: system cost column (View 1 + sponsor labour)

target: Comparison $0.5B vs original $1.92B is not like-for-like
finding: The headline sets the lowest zero-based figure (CFG-1 licensing, View 1 cash, founder unpaid, no investment) against the original MD-5 full-administration operating figure, which counts salaried roles. Compare like with like. Full administration: CFG-5 View 3 $1.20B vs MD-5 $1.92B, about 37% lower, not 74%. Licensing: CFG-1 View 3 $1.04B vs MD-6 $0.96B, so the zero-based licensing figure is actually higher than the original's. Most of the apparent improvement comes from changing the view, founder treatment and configuration, not from zero-based efficiency.
proposed_correction: Publish a bridge table from $1.92B to $0.5B that attributes the change to: configuration change, founder-at-zero-cash, shared-cost exclusion, workload re-estimation, and fee basis. Headline the like-for-like View 3 comparisons.
change_or_reason: Comparison restated on matching views and scope (20, 00)

target: Founder opportunity cost valued at $200/h replacement wage
finding: View 2 values founder time at a market wage ($200/h x 400 h = $80k). For an investor, the opportunity cost is the value forgone on the other 29 initiatives, or the cost of a hired GM/CTO with equivalent accountability, which FC-205 puts at $180k for leadership alone. View 1 (the cash headline) also assumes the founder draws no compensation from Unbound. If the founder needs a salary, or the time is redeployed, the cash headline does not hold.
proposed_correction: Show a View 1b in which founder time is paid cash at a market GM/CTO package for the allocated share. Value opportunity cost by the marginal return of competing initiatives, or at least by the FC-205 leadership cost.
change_or_reason: Opportunity cost on other initiatives is not quantifiable from records; stated qualitatively (08)

target: Legal capacity and IP chain (no counsel spend decision; PolyForm Noncommercial components; no Unbound LICENSE or entity)
finding: Owner decision DF-ASR-2026-0D0F authorises no counsel spend, yet FC-008 and FC-304 cost counsel. Negotiating a first enterprise MSA, DPA, SLA, escrow and Nacha TPSP terms without counsel is not credible for a buyer. Most shared components carry PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0. Unbound has no LICENSE file and no contracting entity, so a buyer's IP and counterparty diligence fails until intercompany licences and an entity exist.
proposed_correction: Treat counsel as mandatory before the first sale. Add an intercompany IP licence, entity formation and first-MSA negotiation (about $30-80k one-time) to development investment, and resolve the owner-decision conflict explicitly.
change_or_reason: Conflict with DF-ASR-2026-0D0F recorded as OD-ZB-02

target: Monte Carlo scope (Analysis.fs mcBreakEven/mcCost)
finding: The Monte Carlo varies only operating parameters. It holds fee level, sponsor count (fixed at 1), sponsor size, CAC, churn and time to revenue constant. So its P10-P90 break-even band ($0.55-0.88B for CFG-5) leaves out the commercial uncertainties that dominate investor risk. The severe named scenario ($10.2M View 1 at $500M) also shows that automation rates, which have never been measured because no product runs, can move cost by an order of magnitude.
proposed_correction: Add commercial distributions (fee 5-25 bps by configuration, sponsor size, churn, months to revenue, CAC) and report the probability of reaching break-even within 5 years, not only break-even assets.
change_or_reason: Sponsor size and fee handled by grids; MC limitation stated (19)

target: Market beta of AUA-based revenue
finding: Revenue is linear in assets while cost is driven by accounts, so market drawdowns cut straight into margin. At $1B, a 30% decline takes 76% of View 1 margin and turns View 2 negative. At the $0.5B headline, any decline produces a loss. DAF assets also fall through grant payouts (typically about 15-25% a year at national sponsors), which must be refilled by contributions.
proposed_correction: Quote break-even at a stressed asset level (e.g. 25-30% drawdown), or add a minimum-fee floor (the MinimumCommitment pricing already exists in Revenue.fs) to the base case.
change_or_reason: Asset-decline stress reported; per-account floors recommended (17)

target: Upside not modelled: implementation fees and AUA growth
finding: No one-time implementation or migration fee is modelled, although institutional buyers routinely pay one, and onboarding costs about $160-200k per sponsor. Organic AUA growth from contributions and markets, and contractual fee escalators, are also absent. Both understate revenue, as long as the buyer accepts them.
proposed_correction: Add an implementation fee (e.g. $25-150k per sponsor, or cost-plus migration) and an optional AUA growth or escalator assumption, and show their effect on payback separately.
change_or_reason: Implementation fees recommended in revenue design (17); not in break-even (conservative)

target: Engineering staffing floor (2 dedicated engineers from 100 accounts)
finding: ENG is the largest cash line ($425k at $500M). It is driven by the 3-named-engineer change-control rule and the 0.6 FTE dedication threshold, not by load: 1,723 h with 314 h from the founder. A contracted part-time independent reviewer who covers the non-author approvals, plus one dedicated engineer, could meet CNV-PLT-010 at lower cost, if auditors accept an external approver. This finding cuts the other way from the founder-availability finding and depends on it.
proposed_correction: Test a configuration of 1 dedicated engineer plus 1 fractional reviewer (about 150-250 h/yr) and record auditor acceptance as the gating assumption.
change_or_reason: Engineering re-derived after review (4,131 h -> 4 FTE); author+2 rule shown non-binding (policy-levers.csv)

target: Non-monotonic marginal sponsor cost (sponsor-unit-economics.csv)
finding: The marginal View 1 cost of adding a sponsor falls from $146k ($250M) to $98k ($500M), then jumps to $243k ($1B). These are staffing-step artefacts of the 2→3 sponsor comparison at fixed account totals, not economics. The 'minimum viable sponsor $75-100M' conclusion therefore depends on where the step thresholds fall.
proposed_correction: Report the marginal cost averaged over a range of base sizes (or over step positions) and give minimum viable size as a range with its step sensitivity.
change_or_reason: REV-A: marginal sponsor cost averaged over four sponsors

target: Break-even grid resolution (accountGrid 100..2M, 70 log points)
finding: Successive grid points differ by about 15.5%. Break-even values are grid points, which explains repeated values such as $509.27M, $587.87M and $678.60M across configurations, so headline precision of two significant figures overstates accuracy. The Monte Carlo grid is coarser still: 28 points, about 43% steps.
proposed_correction: Interpolate between grid points (or bisect) for headline break-even, and round headlines to ±15%.
change_or_reason: Grid resolution ~15.5%; stated in 01 and 18

target: model-outputs/vetting-alternatives.csv; Beneficium.fs vetting; OA-CHR-002/003
finding: The 180-day automated re-evaluation adds no detection value in the model. Hybrid expected false negatives (1.749 per 1k charities) are identical to Continuous monitoring alone (1.749). The extra cost (+$1.8k per 1k charities; +$17.7k at 10k) buys only the policy flag meets_180_day_validity. The vetting comparison also ignores OA-CHR-002, the transaction-time status check at approval and release, which already catches published revocations at the moment of exposure.
proposed_correction: Model the 180-day step as a control with its own detection term: share of stale-source charities x probability that fresh evidence is obtained. Credit the transaction-time check in pFn. If the step only re-reads the same sources, record it as ECHELON-POLICY with zero risk reduction, and let the owner decide on Continuous plus grant-time check plus targeted refresh of stale-source charities.
change_or_reason: REV-A: vetting distinguishes stale-feed events; hybrid differs from continuous

target: beneficium-parameters BNP-047/BNP-055; vetting pFn
finding: False-negative exposure counts the publication-lag window (source_latency_days 45) as taxable-distribution exposure. Under Rev. Proc. 2018-32, sponsoring organizations generally may rely on IRS Tax Exempt Organization Search and BMF status until a revocation is published, unless they had knowledge or were responsible. Grants made before publication therefore carry little 4966 exposure. In the Continuous and Hybrid cases about 98% of modelled pFn comes from that latency term.
proposed_correction: Split ineligibility events into IRS revocations (exposure begins at publication) and non-IRS adverse events (dissolution, fraud, sanctions, state AG action; exposure begins at the event). Apply the 4966 cost only to the post-publication and non-reliance share.
change_or_reason: REV-A: exposure from publication (Rev. Proc. 2018-32); grant-time check modelled

target: beneficium-parameters BNP-055 false_negative_cost
finding: A single cost per false negative ($2.5k base, labelled as the 20% 4966 tax) mixes the wrong mechanics. The 4966 first-tier tax is abatable under IRC 4962 for reasonable cause and correction, because 4962(b) includes subchapter G, which overstates routine cases. At the same time it understates the tail: a grant to a sanctioned or terror-linked charity (OFAC strict civil liability), or a fraud charity with press exposure. The fund-manager 5% tax (cap $10k) under 4966(a)(2) is also not separated.
proposed_correction: Use two or three event classes: routine revoked or dissolved recipient (abatable; recovery labour, typically under $1k); disqualified recipient with no abatement (20% x grant); sanctions or fraud tail (low probability, $50k-$500k incl. counsel and voluntary self-disclosure). Report expected value and P95 separately.
change_or_reason: 4962 abatement noted in 15; single FN cost retained with wide range

target: Beneficium compliance_rate BNP-041 vs roles.csv compliance fractional rate
finding: Vetting labour is costed at $67.69/h (BNP-041). The staffing model buys the same compliance hours at $190/h x 1.1 availability premium = $209/h. Vetting-alternative labour is therefore understated about 3x relative to how the headline model actually pays for compliance work.
proposed_correction: Use one compliance rate source across Beneficium and staffing, either the marginal pool rate or an explicit dedicated-hire rate.
change_or_reason: REV-A: Beneficium compliance rate base $120/h (blend)

target: Staffing.fs minNamed COMPLIANCE=1; headline-staffing named_persons
finding: The compliance pool has one named person and no backup, at every scale shown. CO-018 itself specifies a backup approver for sanctions dispositions with a same-day to 2-business-day SLA. The same person is the OFAC compliance officer, the eligibility-exception adjudicator and the 4966 remediation owner. One absence stalls payment release on any potential match. Key-person and segregation-of-duties failure.
proposed_correction: Set min_named for COMPLIANCE to 2 (the backup may be a sponsor compliance officer under documented delegation, or an external sanctions specialist on retainer). Add a backup retainer.
change_or_reason: REV-A: compliance minimum two named persons

target: Staffing.fs fractional/dedicated decision; roles compliance dedicate_threshold 0.6
finding: The model chooses fractional compliance at $209/h even where a dedicated hire is clearly cheaper. At $500M, 794 h costs $165.9k fractional, against $121.8k for a 1.0 FTE dedicated compliance analyst, who also gives continuous ownership. The 0.6 FTE dedicate threshold is not cost-based: break-even is about 0.40 FTE at these rates. Over-costed in that direction.
proposed_correction: Select the mode by minimum cost (with hire_step 0.5 allowed), not a fixed FTE threshold. Keep a fractional senior or counsel layer for judgment calls.
change_or_reason: REV-A: least-cost fractional vs dedicated

target: CO-042/CO-047; OA-TEC-017/018; Staffing criticalPools
finding: Segregation of duties is modelled only as a head count in the OPS, AUTH and FINANCE pools. The dominant fraud and integrity risk in a 2-3-engineer organisation is engineering privileged access. Engineers who can read and write production data, payee bank details or the generated ACH/positive-pay files can bypass every application-level dual control. The founder is simultaneously owner, executive, engineer and approver. No independent (non-engineering) review of privileged sessions, database changes or payment-file integrity is costed. SOC 1 ITGC testing will focus here.
proposed_correction: Add controls and costs: (1) just-in-time privileged access with session logging (about $3-10k/yr tooling); (2) weekly review of privileged-access and database-change logs by the compliance owner or sponsor (2 h/week, about 100 h/yr); (3) payment-file control totals and hash independently confirmed by the sponsor in the bank portal before release; (4) founder excluded from approving his own production changes.
change_or_reason: REV-A: FC-015 independent privileged-access review

target: OA-TEC-001; roles engineering min_fraction 'named security/on-call owner'; results ENG 2 dedicated + founder
finding: On-call is priced as 19.6 min/day of review, staffed by 2 dedicated engineers plus a founder with a 400 h cap. If any 24x7 response commitment is made, each engineer is on call for about 26 weeks a year, with no stipend, no follow-the-sun coverage and no cover for absence. That is not sustainable and is a retention risk. Conversely, 24x7 human response is not legally required: grants are not time-critical intraday if payment release fails closed.
proposed_correction: Make an explicit owner decision: business-hours support plus extended December and bank-cutoff windows, fail-closed release and automatic pause, after-hours best effort. Price an on-call stipend (about $5-10k per engineer per year) or an MSP/MDR after-hours tier. Do not sell a 24x7 RTO SLA at 2-3 engineers.
change_or_reason: REV-A: FC-017 on-call compensation

target: fixed-costs FC-009/FC-010; OA-TEC-003
finding: Detection tooling is underfunded. FC-010 ($3k) covers SAST and dependency scanning only. There is no SIEM or managed detection and response, no endpoint detection, device management or phishing-resistant MFA for workforce devices, and security monitoring is 55 h/yr of triage. SOC 2 CC6/CC7 and cyber underwriters (MFA, EDR and backup attestations) expect these. With 2-3 engineers, MDR is the only realistic route to out-of-hours detection.
proposed_correction: Add a line: MDR/SIEM-lite (cloud-native alerting plus MDR vendor) $15-40k/yr; endpoint detection, device management and hardware keys about $1-2k per person per year.
change_or_reason: REV-A: FC-016 MDR/endpoint

target: CO-052; roles engineering; FC-105
finding: The named security owner is budgeted at 100 h/yr, a fraction of an engineer, with no security specialist anywhere in the model. That one person also owns the written information security program under 201 CMR 17, pen-test remediation, vendor security reviews, incident command and quarterly reports to the audit committee. For a platform preparing payment files for multiple sponsors this is thin. Institutional due-diligence questionnaires ask for a named CISO or vCISO.
proposed_correction: Budget a fractional vCISO at 150-250 h/yr ($200-275/h), or explicitly assign and train one of the engineers with protected time (about 0.15 FTE).
change_or_reason: Security owner floor kept at 0.1 FTE; MDR and vCISO-capable engineers assumed; flagged in 25

finding: The cost of a breach or incident beyond labour is unpriced. A security incident costs 24 engineering hours plus 8 ops hours. Forensics beyond the $5k retainer, breach counsel, notification and credit monitoring, sponsor indemnities, and the insurance retention or deductible ($10-50k typical) are all missing. The vendor's statutory duty is usually to notify the data owner (the sponsor), but the MSA will shift resident-notification costs to the vendor. A breach-counsel retainer is mentioned in control-obligations-notes but not priced.
proposed_correction: Add expected retained loss: P(notifiable breach) 2-5%/yr x (retention $25k + uninsured items such as betterment, lost revenue and contractual credits, $25-75k), plus a breach-counsel panel through the insurer. Add a stress scenario: one breach of 50k records at about $150-250 per record gross, with insurer limits tested.
change_or_reason: REV-A: FC-018 expected breach cost

target: FC-001/FC-002/FC-003 insurance
finding: Insurance is priced at $1M-type limits with no quote: cyber $15k, E&O $12k, crime $8k. Institutional sponsors and ODFIs commonly require $3-5M technology E&O and cyber, plus crime with third-party (client property) and funds-transfer-fraud or social-engineering coverage. On the other side, tech E&O and cyber are usually written as one combined policy, so two separate premiums may double-count base fees. Insurers also need a formed entity; the licensor LLC is not formed.
proposed_correction: Price a combined tech E&O and cyber policy at $3-5M ($25-60k), crime with a third-party and social-engineering endorsement ($8-20k), and D&O if outside investors or board ($5-15k). Obtain broker indications before relying on them.
change_or_reason: REV-A: insurance ranges raised

target: fixed-costs FC-005 activation vendor_controls; configurations CFG-1/2/6
finding: SOC 1 is activated only where the vendor runs controls (CFG-3/4/5/7). In CFG-1, CFG-2 and CFG-6 the platform is still the sponsor's fund ledger, fee and NAV calculator, reconciliation engine and payment-file generator. Its automated application controls and ITGCs are relevant to the sponsor's financial statements whoever performs the manual steps (AU-C 402). Sponsor auditors will request a SOC 1 or perform their own testing at higher sponsor cost. Licensing-only configurations look $44.5k plus 120 h cheaper than they are.
proposed_correction: Activate SOC 1 for every configuration in which the platform is the system of record, possibly with a reduced scope. Alternatively, model a per-sponsor user-auditor testing cost borne by sponsors.
change_or_reason: REV-A: SOC 1 in licensing configurations

finding: SOC 1 and SOC 2 are priced as independent engagements ($72k combined), alongside a 50%-allocated shared assurance programme ($45k). One firm performing both examinations over a common ITGC control set normally discounts the second report and shares testing. Some evidence collection in FC-105 overlaps OA-TEC-020 (80 h of SOC evidence support).
proposed_correction: Price a bundled SOC 1 plus SOC 2 engagement (about 15-25% lower) and remove the overlap between FC-105 and OA-TEC-020 evidence hours.
change_or_reason: Bundled SOC engagement is a cost-down option (low case covers it)

target: CO-022 OFAC independent testing; CO-027 Nacha audit; FC-007; owner direction DF-ASR-2026-0D0F
finding: Independent testing of the sanctions programme is costed as 16 internal hours. With a single fractional compliance owner, nobody is 'independent of the audited activities'. In addition, owner direction DF-ASR-2026-0D0F authorizes no independent-review spend, which conflicts with the SOC, pen-test, Nacha-audit and OFAC-testing lines in the model. The Nacha audit fee ($15k) is likely high: payments associations commonly perform TPSP Rules Compliance Audits for less, and the requirement to audit by December 31 does not mandate a CPA.
proposed_correction: Fold OFAC programme testing into the external Nacha audit or the SOC scope (an incremental $3-8k), or use the sponsor's internal audit. Reprice the Nacha audit at $5-10k. Record the conflict with the owner direction as a blocking decision rather than a cost assumption.
change_or_reason: REV-A: Nacha audit base lowered to $10k; independent sanctions testing via external line noted

target: OA-CMP-001 sanctions alert rate (exception 0.0009 per screening)
finding: The sanctions alert rate of 0.09% of screenings (about 23 alerts/yr at 2,000 accounts) is optimistic for fuzzy name screening of donors, successors and thousands of charity names, especially with delta re-screening on every list update. The alert workload may be several times higher until match rules are tuned. The driver also counts screenings per account only, not per active charity or payor.
proposed_correction: Use 0.3-1% in the first year, falling to 0.1-0.3% after tuning. Add a per-active-charity screening driver. Validate in a pilot against the actual list vendor.
change_or_reason: Alert rate in sensitivity via exception_mult; measurement priority (25)

target: CO-026/CO-028; ZBP-033 platform_creates_ach_files
finding: Only TPSP status is modelled. If Unbound transmits files to the ODFI under its own agreement, or for several sponsors through one channel, it becomes a Third-Party Sender. A TPS takes on warranty and indemnity liability for its Originators' entries, an annual risk assessment it cannot delegate (CO-028), ODFI underwriting and exposure limits, and Nacha registration through the ODFI. That changes capital, insurance and legal cost materially. The model has no switch for this.
proposed_correction: Make 'no TPS' a design invariant: the sponsor is the Originator, files are released through the sponsor's ODFI credentials, and Unbound has no ODFI agreement. Otherwise add a TPS scenario (risk assessment, higher crime and E&O limits, return-liability reserve and counsel).
change_or_reason: TPS vs TPSP status: open question OQ-ZB-03 for ODFI/counsel

target: Infrastructure C1 deployment; OA-TEC-005/006; CO-020
finding: Disaster recovery in the default C1 deployment depends on same-region, provider-managed database backups (free up to provisioned size, locally redundant by default). These sit in the same tenant and subscription that a compromised admin credential or ransomware actor could delete. No immutable or cross-account backup and no geo-redundant backup is priced. Ten-year OFAC and recordkeeping retention (CO-020, CO-015) and the sponsor's books depend on it.
proposed_correction: In C1 add geo-redundant database backup, an immutable or locked vault or logically air-gapped copy in a separate subscription with separate admins, and quarterly restore-to-alternate-region tests. A warm region (C2) can stay optional.
change_or_reason: REV-A: FC-019 immutable off-region backups

target: Deployment C2 warm DR region; CO-060
finding: Not over-engineered as stated, but worth confirming as a cost_down: a warm DR region is not legally required. A regional outage delays grants by hours to days, which creates no 4966 or Nacha breach, and contribution timing for donor deductions is fixed by the donor's transfer, not by platform posting. The real continuity control is CO-060, under which the sponsor can approve and pay through its own bank channel and see verified balances if the vendor fails. That should be drilled (8 h/yr is light) rather than met with a second region.
proposed_correction: Keep C2 optional and sold as a contractual add-on. Fund a sponsor-side manual payment fallback drill (about 16-24 h/yr across vendor and sponsor) and a documented export of balances and payees refreshed daily to the sponsor.
change_or_reason: C1 (no warm DR) is the base; C2 optional

target: Key-person: founder; ZBP-016; min_named_engineering met by founder
finding: Key-person risk is acknowledged but not costed or mitigated. The founder is the third engineer used to meet author-plus-two, the commercial lead, contract owner and in practice the security owner, with 400 h/yr spread across about 30 initiatives. Sponsors' vendor-risk processes will require source-code and data escrow, documented runbooks, succession, and possibly key-person insurance. Losing the founder leaves the platform without a qualified change approver and with no one able to sign SOC management assertions.
proposed_correction: Add source-code and data escrow ($3-8k/yr), key-person life and disability cover ($2-5k), and runbook and succession documentation hours (40 h/yr). Treat 'standalone without founder' (CFG-7) as needing a third paid engineer or reviewer, not a 40 h retainer.
change_or_reason: REV-B: FC-022 key-person continuity

target: CO-047 / ZBP-043 author-plus-two change approval
finding: Two non-author approvers for control-relevant changes is ECHELON-POLICY (CNV-PLT-010), not a SOC 1 or SOC 2 requirement. Auditors accept one independent, competent reviewer plus automated controls (protected branches, signed builds, CI tests, separate deployment pipeline permission). The rule creates a hard 3-engineer floor, which is the model's main reason to involve the founder or a retainer. The parameter is labelled VERIFIED-FACT/high, but it only verifies that the policy exists, not that it is needed.
proposed_correction: Offer author-plus-one, with a second approver only for payment-file, ledger-posting and authority modules, as a policy alternative. Relabel ZBP-043 as a policy choice (ASSUMPTION/owner decision).
change_or_reason: Policy lever shows author+2 non-binding at current engineering workload; recorded as owner policy choice

target: ZBP-024..026 vs OA-TEC-004
finding: Security incidents are modelled twice, inconsistently. Activity OA-TEC-004 gives 4 incidents/yr x 25 h (100 h), and incidentSpecs separately adds 1 incident/yr x 24 h engineering plus 8 h ops. The basis for each is unstated, and the headline claim of '1 security incident/yr' is not what the model actually charges.
proposed_correction: Keep one source: either a severity mix (e.g. 4 minor at 8 h and 0.5 major at 120 h incl. ops) or the activity row. Document which is used.
change_or_reason: REV-A: duplicated security incident hours removed from simulation

target: CO-030 Nacha data security; CO-049 GLBA
finding: Two citations are applied too broadly in one direction and too narrowly in the other. CO-030 (Nacha supplementing data security) applies only above 2M ACH entries a year; Unbound volume is far below that, so the obligation is contractual or good practice, not Nacha-mandated, although SOC 2 requires the same encryption anyway. CO-049 dismisses GLBA because the nonprofit sponsor is outside FTC jurisdiction. But Echelon Foundry is a for-profit entity within FTC jurisdiction, and whether it is itself a 'financial institution' processing financial data is not analysed.
proposed_correction: Reclassify CO-030 as RISK-BASED/CONTRACTUAL below threshold. Add the vendor-side GLBA question to the counsel list. If it applies, the Safeguards Rule requires a Qualified Individual, annual board report and FTC notice within 30 days for events affecting 500+ consumers, largely satisfied by the 201 CMR 17 program.
change_or_reason: Citation scope notes passed to control-obligations register review (25)

target: fixed-costs.csv FC-009/FC-010; infrastructure-notes.md s6 exclusions
finding: The cloud bill is not material: about $12.5k/yr, or 1.4% of View 1 cash ($914.5k at $250M CFG-1). The non-labour technology services around it are what is underpriced. Security monitoring has no SIEM or managed detection (MDR) line. FC-010 covers only code and dependency scanning. Yet OA-TEC-003 says triage 'could be outsourced MDR', and SOC 2 CC7 plus sponsor due diligence expect centralised security event monitoring with retained evidence.
proposed_correction: Add FC line 'SIEM / MDR' at low $8k, base $20k, high $50k per year (cloud-native SIEM ingestion plus a small-business MDR service), or show that OA-TEC-003 hours replace it. Keep it separate from FC-010.
change_or_reason: Infrastructure ~1% of View 1 (12); labour is the driver

target: FC-009 observability; OA-TEC-001
finding: FC-009 at $6k assumes observability is a paging SaaS bolted onto an existing stack. No stack exists: the owner deferred all monitoring, logging, tracing and alerting on 2026-11-25, Aegis does fault capture only, and Vigila was refuted as an observability system. OA-TEC-001 (19.6 min/day) assumes SLOs, alerts and runbooks that nobody has built or costed.
proposed_correction: Raise FC-009 to low $6k, base $12k, high $30k (APM or error tracking, paging for 3-4 people, uptime/synthetics, status page). Add a one-time build of 150-300 h for instrumentation, SLO dashboards, alert routing and runbooks to FC-301, plus about 50 h/yr upkeep to TEC-001.
change_or_reason: REV-B: FC-009 raised to 6/18/40k

target: infrastructure-parameters.csv platform_fixed_monthly; infrastructure-notes s6
finding: No cloud support plan is priced, although it is listed as UNKNOWN in the exclusions. A payments-adjacent platform with a 1-hour on-call SLO and a single managed PostgreSQL cluster needs vendor escalation, and sponsor due diligence usually asks about it.
proposed_correction: Add FC 'cloud support plan' at low $1.2k, base $3.6k, high $12k (Azure Standard about $100/mo; AWS Business max($100, 10% of bill); a higher response tier as the high case).
change_or_reason: Support plan UNKNOWN; within infra_mult range

target: ZBI-004 Front Door Premium; DDoS
finding: The floor uses Azure Front Door Premium ($330/mo) only to get managed WAF rules, and the 35% non-production uplift is applied to it as well. The cheaper options give an equivalent result: Front Door Standard with custom rules ($40), or AWS WAF/CloudFront (about $15). In the other direction, do not add paid DDoS products (Azure DDoS Network Protection about $2,944/mo; AWS Shield Advanced $3,000/mo with a 1-year commitment). Edge-terminated L3/L4 protection plus a WAF is sufficient at this risk and scale.
proposed_correction: Set the base platform_fixed_monthly to the Standard/AWS-equivalent (about $120) and keep Premium as the high case. Exclude Front Door from the non-production base. Record explicitly that paid DDoS is out of scope unless a sponsor contract requires it.
change_or_reason: Front Door Premium kept as base for managed WAF on a financial app; Standard is the low case

target: Analysis.fs mcCost / evaluate (iv = infraVals at Base); ZBP-034 infra_mult
finding: Monte Carlo and the tornado analysis always evaluate infrastructure at its base parameters. Uncertainty enters only through infra_mult (0.7-1.5). The notes, however, show compounded high-case cost per account at 13x base at 1M accounts ($2.27 vs $0.17) and 28x at 100k. The scale-tail risk (identity MAU, SMS, events per account, vCPU per event) therefore never appears in the P90s.
proposed_correction: Draw the infrastructure-parameters.csv rows in the Monte Carlo (correlated with activity_mult), or widen infra_mult to 0.5-4 for retail and payroll scale runs.
change_or_reason: Infrastructure uncertainty via infra_mult only; immaterial to results

target: OA-TEC-005 backup verification and tenant restore; ZBI-022/023 backups
finding: Tenant-scoped restore in a schema-per-sponsor cluster is not a 1-hour monthly check. Managed point-in-time recovery restores the whole server, so a tenant restore means a new server, then a schema extraction, then reconciliation against the append-only, hash-linked ledger and outbox. That needs purpose-built tooling and a 3-8 h exercise. Ten-year immutable (WORM) backups or archives for ransomware and records requirements are also unpriced, because point-in-time retention ends at 35 days.
proposed_correction: One-time 80-200 h to build restore tooling (FC-301). Set OA-TEC-005 to 12 x 4 h (low 2 h, high 8 h). Add an immutable long-term backup or archive line at $0.5k-3k/yr, scaling with stored GB. Also add 4-8 environment-weeks a year of temporary production-scale environments for the OA-TEC-006/015 load tests and the restore targets (+$0.5k-3k/yr); the 35% non-production share does not cover these.
change_or_reason: REV-B: OA-TEC-006 +240 min for tenant-scoped restore testing

target: Infrastructure.fs compute scaling; infrastructure-notes s4 thresholds
finding: The architecture's change point is presented as a vCPU threshold (2 vCores to about 730k accounts at base; about 23k in the high case). Compute will not be the first limit to bind. More likely triggers, in order: (1) the first institutional sponsor contractually demanding a dedicated database, customer-managed key or region (C3), which can happen at sponsor 1; (2) December and year-end batch work (statements, tax receipts, unit/NAV allocations, reconciliation queries) on the same primary as the database-backed queues, since the event model counts only durable events and no read or reporting load; (3) one region, one primary and a deferred observability stack giving an RTO that sponsors will not accept; (4) schema count and migration fan-out above roughly 50-100 sponsors.
proposed_correction: Replace the single vCPU threshold with explicit trigger metrics: queue lag p99 in December, primary CPU above 60% during the statement run, a sponsor isolation clause, and sponsor count above 50. Price a read replica for reporting ($130-250/mo) from about 50k accounts or the first year-end. Run the RM-05 benchmark before acceptance.
change_or_reason: Architecture change points restated in 12

target: Deployment C3; ZBP-032 isolated_db_accounts_threshold
finding: C3 prices each isolated sponsor database at cloud list price only ($5.5k/yr). Each isolated database is in practice another production system. It needs its own migrations, major-version upgrades, restore tests, DR drills, monitoring and key rotation, yet the TECHOPS rows driven per_platform (TEC-005/006/011/015) do not scale with the number of isolated databases.
proposed_correction: Add per-isolated-database engineering of 40-80 h/yr (TEC-005/006/011 share), and note that isolation can be triggered by contract below 50k accounts.
change_or_reason: C3 operational overhead noted; contractual trigger

target: ZBI-020 retention_years; Infrastructure.fs storage; ZBI-041 egress
finding: Several storage and egress details are mis-scaled but small. (a) Retention: 7 years are kept online, but records must be retained 10 years after the transaction, and an append-only, hash-chained ledger is in practice never pruned, so online data grows without limit. (b) Storage is priced at steady state (7 x annual volume) even in year 1, which overstates it early. (c) Stepped SKUs (2 to 4 vCores, 128 GB to 512 GB to 4 TB) are priced continuously, e.g. 0.74 extra vCPU at 1M accounts. (d) Egress of 15 MB per account-year may be low for a .NET WebAssembly bundle (several MB compressed, re-downloaded after each of about 50 releases a year).
proposed_correction: Model storage as a cumulative year-by-year schedule with retention of at least 10 years and archive tiering. Use stepped SKUs. Raise egress_gb_per_acct high to 0.15.
change_or_reason: Small storage/egress details; immaterial

target: ZBI-004 base logs 15 GB/mo; ZBI-028
finding: Base log volume of 15 GB/mo excludes the audit logs that SOC 2 and sponsors will ask for: pgaudit on regulated tables, WAF/Front Door access logs, and identity sign-in logs. Each can exceed application logs. At $2.30/GB in the Log Analytics analytics tier, 50-100 GB/mo costs about $100-220/mo more.
proposed_correction: Raise base logs to 40-60 GB/mo, with a design rule to send audit/WAF logs to Basic/Auxiliary tiers.
change_or_reason: Audit-log volume within log high case

target: Database architecture: role per sponsor, database-backed queues
finding: Two operational costs of the chosen PostgreSQL pattern are missing. (1) A role per sponsor fragments connection pools: a pool per role means connections grow with sponsors x pool size, so a pooler is needed (PgBouncer built-in on Azure; RDS Proxy about $22/mo on AWS). (2) Queue, outbox and timer tables churn (insert, update, delete), unlike the append-only ledger. They need autovacuum tuning and bloat monitoring, and the 1.25 overhead factor assumes append-only rows.
proposed_correction: Add a pooler line (AWS) and 20-40 h/yr of queue and database hygiene to OA-TEC-011. Include connection count and bloat in the RM-05 benchmark.
change_or_reason: Connection pooling and per-role costs recorded as architecture risks (24)

target: OA-TEC-010 two-approver review; Workload.fs authMinutes; Simulation arrivals
finding: The two-approver review is costed wrongly in two ways. (1) The second approval goes to the 'authorizer' role, which is the AUTH pool at controller rates, so 0.3 x 40 min = 12 min of one reviewer, instead of to engineers. CNV-PLT-010 requires two non-author engineering approvers per control-relevant change. (2) A volume of 300 changes a year is low for an AI-assisted codebase that inserted about 288k lines in 6 days, with 376 Unbound commits over the same period. AI-generated pull requests are larger and need deeper review.
proposed_correction: Model OA-TEC-010 as ENG minutes = changes x 2 approvers x 45 min, plus author rework at 20%. Use base 500 changes (high 1,500). Route nothing from TEC-010 to AUTH.
change_or_reason: REV-A: review routed to engineering; change volume 600/yr

target: ZBP-043 min_named_engineering = 3; Staffing.fs named persons
finding: The rule of author plus two non-author approvers is met only by counting the founder as the third engineer. Every control-relevant change then needs all three people. Each person is absent 25 business days a year, and the founder has 400 h for Unbound across 30 initiatives, so releases and emergency fixes will regularly be blocked. Alternatively the founder becomes the routine reviewer, which consumes founder hours the model does not count. A security fix on a control-relevant module cannot wait for the founder.
proposed_correction: Require 4 named engineering approvers (3 dedicated + founder), or 3 dedicated plus a contracted, access-provisioned reviewer retainer of 100-200 h/yr. Add an emergency-change procedure with retrospective second approval.
change_or_reason: Engineering now 4 dedicated; founder not needed as third approver

target: Simulation.fs capacity (weekends 0); OA-TEC-001 sla_hours 1
finding: On-call is effectively unmodelled. The simulation gives every pool zero capacity at weekends and converts the 1-hour SLA into one business day. Weekend and night incidents (including around 31 December and the ACH cut-offs) therefore wait for Monday, and no standby cost appears. With 2 engineers plus a founder, 24/7 cover is a 1-in-3 rota, which tends to burn people out and drive turnover, and no pager stipend or time off in lieu is included.
proposed_correction: Add an on-call cost: stipend $300-600 per person-week of cover (52 weeks), plus out-of-hours incident time at 1.5x. Reduce productive hours by 3-5% for time off in lieu. Model a 4-person rota as the sustainable minimum.
change_or_reason: REV-A: FC-017 on-call; sub-day SLA approximation documented

target: OA-TEC-012 integration maintenance; OA-CHR-010
finding: Integration maintenance is scaled per sponsor (20 x 2 h = 40 h per sponsor-year). The cited evidence prices it per integration ($9.4k, about 63-80 h, per custom integration per year), and most integrations are platform-level and shared. These include: the ODFI/Nacha file origination; the payment partners Chariot, then PayPal; the external investment manager or custodian; identity and bank verification (Stripe, Persona, Plaid/Financial Connections); email and SMS; and the accounting export. Each has API deprecations, certificate and SFTP key rotation, recertification and rule changes. With one sponsor, the model carries about 45 h/yr for all of them.
proposed_correction: Add a platform-level row: about 8-12 integrations x 40-80 h/yr (base 10 x 60 = 600 h). Keep per-sponsor work for sponsor-specific mappings only (20 h).
change_or_reason: REV-A: OA-TEC-023 shared integration upkeep

target: TECHOPS inventory: absence of defect remediation and enhancement
finding: No activity covers fixing production defects or the sponsor-driven change backlog. OA-TEC-019 (40 h/sponsor) covers diagnosis only. OA-TEC-011 (246 h) covers migrations, upgrades and flag hygiene. A new, AI-generated financial system of about 27k F# lines will have escaped defects in its first 2-3 years. Each fix passes through test, the two-approver review and the release rings, and ledger defects also need correction postings. Industry norms put sustaining engineering at 15-20% of build effort per year.
proposed_correction: Add OA-TEC-022 'Defect remediation and sustaining change' at low 400 h, base 900 h, high 1,800 h per year, per platform (equivalent to 7-14% of a $1.5-1.94M build at $118/h). Scale +10% per additional sponsor for configuration requests.
change_or_reason: REV-A: OA-TEC-022 defect correction

target: TECHOPS / COMPLIANCE: regulatory change implementation
finding: No engineering line implements regulatory change. Known changes already in flight include: the 2025 federal tax law's charitable changes from 2026 (0.5%-of-AGI floor for itemizers, a cap on the deduction benefit, and a non-itemizer deduction that excludes DAF gifts), which affect donor statements and receipts; the Nacha 2026 fraud-monitoring rule phases; and the still-pending Treasury DAF regulations. Recurring changes include IRS form and schema years, OFAC list formats and state unclaimed-property rules.
proposed_correction: Add OA-TEC-023 'Regulatory change implementation' at low 80 h, base 200 h, high 500 h per year, per platform, including a two-approver review.
change_or_reason: REV-B: OA-TEC-024 regulatory change

target: OA-TEC-007 vulnerability management and dependency updates
finding: OA-TEC-007 comes to about 82 h/yr after the AI factor (12 x 480 min x 0.85). Patching spans several stacks: the .NET LTS cadence (.NET 8 support ends November 2026, so a .NET 10 migration falls in year 1); the F# compiler and WebAssembly toolchain; the Limen TypeScript kernel and its npm tree; container base images; PostgreSQL major-version upgrades through a pilot tool (Strata 0.1.1); and the release churn of Echelon components (Praxis had 40 tags in 4 months). Critical CVEs arrive in bursts with a 168 h SLA, not evenly through the year.
proposed_correction: Raise TEC-007 to a base of 16 h/month (high 30), and add 80-160 h one-time for each LTS or PostgreSQL major upgrade every 2 years. Model critical CVEs as incidents.
change_or_reason: REV-B: OA-TEC-007 x1.5

target: FC-101 shared component maintenance; ZBP-016 founder_hours; Echelon reliance
finding: Unbound's dependency on immature Echelon components is costed as founder time that is not cash and capacity that does not exist. Transitus (job queue, schema governance, observability) has no code. Echelon.Execution (2,558 lines) is incubated in Unbound and has not been benchmarked. Strata is a v0.1.1 pilot. Monitoring is absent. Fides supports GitHub sign-in only, and Folio has no PDF engine. Each of these has Unbound as its only consumer, so it is in effect Unbound code. Yet FC-101 ($52.5k share) is founder-performed and excluded from View 1. The founder is also allocated 400 h in staffing, about 450 h of assurance work and roughly 260 h for FC-101, competing for 1,800 h across 30 initiatives.
proposed_correction: Treat Execution, Transitus (or its replacement) and Strata as Unbound engineering: add 300-600 h/yr to ENG, in cash, in View 1. Add a founder-capacity constraint check: Unbound founder hours across staffing, FC-101 and assurance must not exceed the owner's allocation. Make replacing Transitus with mature open-source or managed services an explicit decision.
change_or_reason: Transfer-not-elimination stated (08, 16); Beneficium upkeep in pools

target: Unbound CI/CD, infrastructure as code, signed builds (FC-301; OA-TEC-009)
finding: OA-TEC-009 (signed builds; synthetic, canary and production rings) and OA-TEC-010 (approval enforcement) assume a CI/CD pipeline. Unbound has no CI and no Praxis installation, and no repository runs SAST, dependency or secret scanning. The availability brief also rules out Terraform. Without infrastructure as code, DR rebuilds and SOC 2 change-management evidence depend on manual console changes.
proposed_correction: One-time 300-700 h in FC-301 for the pipeline, signing, SBOM, environment promotion and IaC (Bicep/CloudFormation/OpenTofu). Add 60-120 h/yr upkeep. Budget CI minutes beyond the Team allowance ($20-100/mo).
change_or_reason: CI/CD build one-time noted in 16

target: Simulation incident handling; TEC-002/TEC-019 per_sponsor drivers; staffing-thresholds.csv ENG
finding: Incident load is mis-shaped in both directions. (a) OA-TEC-002 (50 h) and TEC-019 (40 h) scale linearly per sponsor. In a shared monolith most incidents are platform-wide and are triaged once; only communication scales with sponsors. This drives the steep ENG thresholds (PG-INST 6 FTE at 7,500 accounts; PG-HNW 7 at 40k, i.e. 20 sponsors). (b) Seeded incidents must be completed within one business day, and adding people is assumed to shorten the fix linearly, which inflates simulated headcount. (c) The other way: the 50 h of TEC-002 is spread across every day of the year, so incident lumpiness at 1-2 sponsors disappears.
proposed_correction: Split TEC-002 into a platform part (base 40 h + 3 incidents x 16 h) and a per-sponsor communication part (8 h). Model incidents as lumps with a 3-5 business-day completion target and a cap on concurrent engineers. Re-derive the ENG thresholds.
change_or_reason: Per-sponsor incident scaling retained (conservative); noted

target: roles.csv engineering cost; hiring
finding: The engineering cost of $212.4k loaded ($118/h x 1,800 h) is a generic software engineer rate. The roles need F#/.NET, PostgreSQL internals, payments and SOC 2 security, and a 1-in-3 on-call rota. The F# talent pool is small, so expect recruiter fees (20-25% of first-year salary), longer vacancies and a retention premium. The model has no recruiting, onboarding or turnover cost for engineers.
proposed_correction: Raise the base to about $235k (high $280k). Add engineering recruiting and turnover of $15k-30k per engineer-year (one replacement every 3-4 years plus a fee) in View 1.
change_or_reason: REV-B: engineering cost base $230k

target: FC-301 / FC-302 development cost vs $1.94M baseline
finding: FC-302's base ($1.5M) is set below the competitive-displacement build baseline ($1.94M) even though no effort records exist. Its rationale says the line counts are output, not effort. FC-301 cash ($0.5M, agent usage plus contract review) omits items still to be built: CI/IaC, observability, donor identity (no Echelon provider), a PDF engine (Folio has none), payment-partner adapters, Transitus's scope, restore tooling, an independent secure-code review of AI-generated control modules, and engineers hired before revenue (months_to_first_revenue 12) if these are not counted as working capital.
proposed_correction: Set the FC-302 base to $1.94M until effort is measured. Itemise FC-301 with the missing build lines (about 1,200-2,500 h, or $140k-300k) plus a secure-code review ($30k-60k). State whether pre-revenue engineer salaries sit in FC-301 or in working capital, and do not count them twice.
change_or_reason: REV-B: FC-302 base $1.94M

target: AI-generated code validation; OA-TEC-021; FC-104
finding: Validating AI-generated code costs more than review time. It needs a maintained test oracle (ledger property tests, reconciliation invariants, mutation testing on control modules) and evaluation runs whenever models or prompts change. finding: The modelled 1,714 h/yr for ENG (2 dedicated plus 314 founder hours, 58.8% utilisation at $250M) is credible only as keep-the-lights-on operations with feature work frozen. target: model/src/ZeroBased/Domain.fs bucket(); configurations.csv CFG-4/CFG-5; activity-loads-reference.csv

target: operational-activities.csv OA-ACN-008 (freq_base 0.5; exception_base 0.8)

target: operational-activities.csv OA-COM-004/007/009/010/011, OA-ACG-006; parameters.csv ZBP-023 new_sponsor_share
finding: Onboarding is annualised at 0.2 new sponsors a year, which turns about 1,150 h of implementation, migration, payee verification, hypercare and calibration (OA-COM-007 500 h, OA-COM-009 367 h, OA-ACG-006 100 h, OA-COM-011 69 h, OA-COM-010 50 h, OA-COM-004 60 h) into about 230 h of steady load. target: model/src/ZeroBased/Staffing.fs staffPool mode selection; roles.csv compliance; headline-staffing.csv COMPLIANCE

target: fixed-costs.csv FC-001, FC-002, FC-003
finding: The insurance premiums ($15k cyber, $12k tech E&O, $8k crime) are consistent with about $1M-2M limits. target: fixed-costs.csv FC-004, FC-005; operational-activities.csv OA-TEC-020, OA-CMP-011
finding: The SOC fees ($27.5k SOC 2 and $44.5k SOC 1) are compliance-automation marketplace vendor claims. Internal effort OA-TEC-020 of 80 h a year is also light: about 300-500 h in year 1 and 150-250 h at steady state.

target: operational-activities.csv OA-TEC-018, OA-TEC-010; parameters.csv ZBP-043 min_named_engineering

target: fixed-costs.csv FC-008 recurring legal counsel; FC-304

It also conflicts with DF-ASR-2026-0D0F (no counsel spend), so the base case relies on spend the owner has not authorised.

target: data/evidence/activity-inventory-notes.md section 6; OA-CMP-003, OA-ACG-005, OA-ACG-007, OA-INV-004, OA-CMP-016
finding: Some inherited requirements create redundant work, and the register keeps all of it at full cost. A daily independent NAV sample (OA-INV-004, 50% x 250 days) checks values Unbound does not compute, and there is an annual affiliation attestation for every account (OA-CMP-016). The model's own notes identify these, but the inputs still apply them.
proposed_correction: Use one error-bound sampling plan, weekly or risk-triggered NAV sampling, and event-driven affiliation confirmation, and reduce the corresponding rows.
change_or_reason: Redundant sampling/reconciliation layers in redesign register (21)

target: data/model-outputs/baseline-comparison.csv; results.md section 3 break-even; headline-scenarios.csv sponsor_hours/sponsor_labour_value

target: fixed-costs.csv FC-012 (activation not_standalone); FC-206
finding: CFG-7 (standalone administrator) drops the sales and marketing programme (FC-012 activation 'not_standalone') with no standalone replacement, so CFG-7 View 1 comes out $25k below CFG-5 ($1.092M against $1.117M at $500M). target: data/model-outputs/infrastructure.csv column ai; operational-activities.csv OA-TEC-021 and AI-ASSISTED rows
finding: Infrastructure prices AI usage at about $24 a year for 1,000 accounts ($193 at 10,000). The design relies on AI for grounded donor answers (OA-ACN-001), exception preparation, the monthly close package (OA-ACG-007), the Form 990 package (OA-ACG-010), and an agent evaluation and change-control regime (OA-TEC-021, 384 h a year), which implies recurring evaluation-suite runs.
